_doc: THE KEEPSAKE stage boss: the geometry contract for src/sprites/boss/keepsake-boss.{png,json} (written by tools/prep_keepsake_boss.py). Units: game px from the boss origin (between the eyes at tilt 0). Tilt: canvas degrees, + = clockwise on screen, so -32 puts the crown toward the ship (screen left). Every head layer is baked rotated about the origin and drawn at the origin: bf(c, key, list, tiltIndex, e.x, e.y). Draw order: face<c> -> eye_<state> -> wound_<state>. face<c> alone is a complete head (half-lidded, seated wound with no fork).

frame.note: the reference head box at tilt 0; atlas frames are cropped to their pixels with offsets from the origin, so read sizes from the layout, not from here

lists.face0: crack WHOLE (phase 1), one frame per tilt
lists.face3: SPLIT OPEN (phase 3: ship meat in the gap)
lists.eye_open: the stare: an attack is coming (catchlight)
lists.eye_empty: phase 3: the mechanism fell out, empty sockets
lists.wound_seat: the fork seated in the split
lists.wound_proud: the tell: the fork pushed up 9 px
lists.wound_brain: phase 3: the larger brain, gaping, no fork
lists.die: split open, empty sockets, the brain, tipping onto its side at tilts [48, 66, 82, 90]
lists.rocker_open: the sleep-eye mechanism at swing angles [-108, -90, -72, -54, -36, -18, 0, 18, 36, 54, 72, 90, 108] (canvas deg about its attach point), lids open
lists.rocker_shut: the same, lids shut (the death clack: PUT TO BED)
lists.crier: [0] whole, [1] broken; origin at its centre
lists.fork: the big fork (thrown / boomerang), tines down, origin at its centre; rotate at runtime (it spins)
lists.mfork: [0] a hanging mobile fork, [1] the drop tell (brighter); origin at the top centre (the thread)

crown.note: ANGLE: full damage at head-local y <= line (phases 1-2) or line3 (phase 3, the split exposes more). top is the crown at tilt 0. Head-local = screen rotated by -tilt about the origin

fork.note: wound_seat/proud have it baked in. entry: px from the fork's top where it goes into the skull

rocker.attach: frame offsets are from the wire end (the bridle apex); draw the wire from perTilt.wire to it. The weight sits 48 px below the apex, so with KB.pLen 58 the apex is 10 px down the wire. Pick the swing frame nearest the pendulum angle (deg, + = clockwise)

source: photos by Matt Arvon of his own unmarked antique doll (D7/D53); not in the repo
